e-5903.knowledge_point: Calculating the Complex Conjugate of a Complex Matrix
e-5903.problem: Find $B=\overline{A},$ where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14045065/assets/25ce0cd375da320d1615cf49f659ec33e4646cf6bc66455198bec5fd591b3dd3.png) What is the value of $b_{11} + b_{23}?$
e-5903.worked_solution:
Taking the complex conjugate of each entry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}4\text{i} & 3-\text{i} & 1+\text{i} \\ 2-2\text{i} & 2-\text{i} & 1+2\text{i} \\ \text{i} & 3\text{i} & 2\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{4\text{i}} & \overset{―}{3-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{1+\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{2-2\text{i}} & \overset{―}{2-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{1+2\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{\text{i}} & \overset{―}{3\text{i}} & \overset{―}{2\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4\text{i} & 3+\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ 2+2\text{i} & 2+\text{i} & 1-2\text{i} \\ -\text{i} & -3\text{i} & -2\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $b_{11} + b_{23} = (-4\textrm{i}) + (1-2\textrm{i}) = 1-6\textrm{i}.$

e-5525.knowledge_point: Computing Components of the Real and Imaginary Parts of a Complex Matrix
e-5525.problem: If ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14045065/assets/3e677aa7f2db1cc637e0566a60813ebae1e2bccf80325106317c1d2b7717c2a5.png) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14045065/assets/67a421166c674275ae14da43962c8e5c8ea37b6a9c8a0548d5b09428b703d831.png) are the real and imaginary parts of the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14045065/assets/fde83769f627e95f5dfe3285bf275ebfe1678710a36c264b6662248063470bb0.png) then what is the value of $ad+eh?$
e-5525.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2-3\text{i} & -5-7\text{i} \\ 1-6\text{i} & 5-9\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-3 & -7 \\ -6 & -9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $a=2,d=5,e=-3$ and $h=-9.$ Therefore,

$$
ad+eh=2 \cdot 5 + (-3) \cdot (-9) = 37.
$$

e-5902.worked_solution:
Multiplying the matrices using the usual method, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 1 & 2\text{i}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ \text{i} & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(-\text{i})\cdot (1+2\text{i})+\text{i}\cdot \text{i} & (-\text{i})\cdot (1-\text{i})+\text{i}\cdot 2 \\ 1\cdot (1+2\text{i})+2\text{i}\cdot \text{i} & 1\cdot (1-\text{i})+2\text{i}\cdot 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(2-\text{i})+(-1) & (-1-\text{i})+2\text{i} \\ (1+2\text{i})+(-2) & (1-\text{i})+4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & -1+\text{i} \\ -1+2\text{i} & 1+3\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
R_1 := \dfrac{1}{\textrm{i}}R_1, \qquad R_2 := R_2 - 2\textrm{i}R_1
$$
e-5526.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A\mathbin{:}$

$$

$$

after.problem: Find $B=\overset{―}{A}$, where $A=[\begin{aligned}7-\text{i} & 6+4\text{i} \\ 7-4\text{i} & 4+9\text{i}\end{aligned}].$ What is the value of ${b}_{12}-{b}_{21}?$
after.worked_solution:
Taking the complex conjugate of each entry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}7-\text{i} & 6+4\text{i} \\ 7-4\text{i} & 4+9\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{7-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{6+4\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{7-4\text{i}} & \overset{―}{4+9\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7+\text{i} & 6-4\text{i} \\ 7+4\text{i} & 4-9\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${b}_{12}-{b}_{21}=(6-4\text{i})-(7+4\text{i})=-1-8\text{i}.$

Taking the complex conjugate of each entry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}-2+\text{i} & 4 & -\text{i} \\ -5\text{i} & 7-5\text{i} & 1 \\ 3-2\text{i} & \text{i} & 0\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{-2+\text{i}} & \overset{―}{4} & \overset{―}{-\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{-5\text{i}} & \overset{―}{7-5\text{i}} & \overset{―}{1} \\ \overset{―}{3-2\text{i}} & \overset{―}{\text{i}} & \overset{―}{0}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2-\text{i} & 4 & \text{i} \\ 5\text{i} & 7+5\text{i} & 1 \\ 3+2\text{i} & -\text{i} & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${b}_{13}+{b}_{31}=\text{i}+(3+2\text{i})=3+3\text{i}.$
history.html:
Taking the complex conjugate of each entry, we get

A―=[−2+i4−i−5i7−5i13−2ii0]―=[−2+i―4―−i―−5i―7−5i―1―3−2i―i―0―]=[−2−i4i5i7+5i13+2i−i0].

Therefore, b13+b31=i+(3+2i)=3+3i.

Your Answer:
3−3i

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Find $B=\overset{―}{A}$, where $A=[\begin{aligned}-3+6\text{i} & 2+7\text{i} \\ 9 & 9-5\text{i}\end{aligned}].$ What is the value of ${b}_{12}+{b}_{22}?$
after.worked_solution:
Taking the complex conjugate of each entry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}-3+6\text{i} & 2+7\text{i} \\ 9 & 9-5\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{-3+6\text{i}} & \overset{―}{2+7\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{9} & \overset{―}{9-5\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3-6\text{i} & 2-7\text{i} \\ 9 & 9+5\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${b}_{12}+{b}_{22}=(2-7\text{i})+(9+5\text{i})=11-2\text{i}.$

after.worked_solution:
Taking the complex conjugate of each entry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}-4-2\text{i} & 7+5\text{i} & 6+6\text{i} \\ -4+5\text{i} & 2-\text{i} & 3 \\ -2-\text{i} & 2-\text{i} & -3\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{-4-2\text{i}} & \overset{―}{7+5\text{i}} & \overset{―}{6+6\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{-4+5\text{i}} & \overset{―}{2-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{3} \\ \overset{―}{-2-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{2-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{-3\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4+2\text{i} & 7-5\text{i} & 6-6\text{i} \\ -4-5\text{i} & 2+\text{i} & 3 \\ -2+\text{i} & 2+\text{i} & 3\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

Find B=A―, where A=[−4−2i7+5i6+6i−4+5i2−i3−2−i2−i−3i]. What is the value of b23+b33?

EXPLANATION

Taking the complex conjugate of each entry, we get

A―=[−4−2i7+5i6+6i−4+5i2−i3−2−i2−i−3i]―=[−4−2i―7+5i―6+6i―−4+5i―2−i―3―−2−i―2−i―−3i―]=[−4+2i7−5i6−6i−4−5i2+i3−2+i2+i3i].

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Complex Conjugate of a Complex Matrix
content.problem:
Find $B=\overset{―}{A}$, where
$A=[\begin{aligned}-4-2\text{i} & 7+5\text{i} & 6+6\text{i} \\ -4+5\text{i} & 2-\text{i} & 3 \\ -2-\text{i} & 2-\text{i} & -3\text{i}\end{aligned}].$
What is the value of ${b}_{23}+{b}_{33}?$
content.worked_solution:
Taking the complex conjugate of each entry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}-4-2\text{i} & 7+5\text{i} & 6+6\text{i} \\ -4+5\text{i} & 2-\text{i} & 3 \\ -2-\text{i} & 2-\text{i} & -3\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{-4-2\text{i}} & \overset{―}{7+5\text{i}} & \overset{―}{6+6\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{-4+5\text{i}} & \overset{―}{2-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{3} \\ \overset{―}{-2-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{2-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{-3\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4+2\text{i} & 7-5\text{i} & 6-6\text{i} \\ -4-5\text{i} & 2+\text{i} & 3 \\ -2+\text{i} & 2+\text{i} & 3\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${b}_{23}+{b}_{33}=3+3\text{i}.$

Question 6
?

If Re(x)=[abcd] and Im(x)=[efgh] are the real and imaginary parts of the matrix A=[−3−9i−7+i−5−2i−4i] then what is the value of bc−ef?

a
44
b
46
c
38
d
31
e
26
Submit

decision.explanation: The real parts give b=−7 and c=−5, while the imaginary coefficients give e=−9 and f=1. Thus bc−ef=(−7)(−5)−(−9)(1)=35+9=44.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem: If $\,\text{Re}(x)=[\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,\text{Im}(x)=[\begin{aligned}e & f \\ g & h\end{aligned}]\,$ are the real and imaginary parts of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-3-9\text{i} & -7+\text{i} \\ -5-2\text{i} & -4\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$ then what is the value of $bc-ef?$
after.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-3-9\text{i} & -7+\text{i} \\ -5-2\text{i} & -4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\ A & =[\begin{aligned}-3-9\text{i} & -7+\text{i} \\ -5-2\text{i} & 0-4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-3 & -7 \\ -5 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-9 & 1 \\ -2 & -4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $b=-7,c=-5,e=-9$ and $f=1.$ Therefore,

$$
bc-ef=(-7)\cdot (-5)-(-9)\cdot 1=44.
$$

decision.explanation: Take the real part of each entry: 1+2i gives 1, 7−6i gives 7, −i gives 0, and 4 gives 4. This matches option b.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem: Find the real part of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 7-6\text{i} \\ -\text{i} & 4\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 7-6\text{i} \\ -\text{i} & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 7-6\text{i} \\ 0-\text{i} & 4+0\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{Re}(A)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}].$

content.problem: Find the real part of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 7-6\text{i} \\ -\text{i} & 4\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 7-6\text{i} \\ -\text{i} & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 7-6\text{i} \\ 0-\text{i} & 4+0\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{Re}(A)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}].$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-2+3\text{i} & -5+2\text{i} \\ 6-7\text{i} & 4-9\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-2 & -5 \\ 6 & 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -7 & -9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}

content.knowledge_point: Computing Components of the Real and Imaginary Parts of a Complex Matrix
content.problem: Find the real part of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-2+3\text{i} & -5+2\text{i} \\ 6-7\text{i} & 4-9\text{i}\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-2+3\text{i} & -5+2\text{i} \\ 6-7\text{i} & 4-9\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-2 & -5 \\ 6 & 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -7 & -9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{Re}(A)=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -5 \\ 6 & 4\end{aligned}].$

after.problem: Find the real part of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2-3\text{i} & 2\text{i} \\ 7 & -9+4\text{i}\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$

For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2-3\text{i} & 2\text{i} \\ 7 & -9+4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2-3\text{i} & 0+2\text{i} \\ 7+0\text{i} & -9+4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 7 & -9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{Re}(A)=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 7 & -9\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 10
after.problem: Find the imaginary part of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}8+\text{i} & 3-4\text{i} \\ 9 & \text{i}\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}8+\text{i} & 3-4\text{i} \\ 9 & \text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8+\text{i} & 3-4\text{i} \\ 9+0\text{i} & 0+\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}8 & 3 \\ 9 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{Im}(A)=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].$

decision.explanation: Using row-by-column multiplication and i²=−1, the four entries are (1−3i)(3−i)+(−1+2i)(−1+i)=−1−13i; (1−3i)(3+i)+(−1+2i)(1−i)=7−5i; (2+2i)(3−i)+(1−i)(−1+i)=8+6i; and (2+2i)(3+i)+(1−i)²=4+6i. This matches option b.

after.problem: If $\,A=[\begin{aligned}1-3\text{i} & -1+2\text{i} \\ 2+2\text{i} & 1-\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,B=[\begin{aligned}3-\text{i} & 3+\text{i} \\ -1+\text{i} & 1-\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$, then $AB=$
after.worked_solution:
Multiplying the matrices using the usual method, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}1-3\text{i} & -1+2\text{i} \\ 2+2\text{i} & 1-\text{i}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3-\text{i} & 3+\text{i} \\ -1+\text{i} & 1-\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(1-3\text{i})(3-\text{i})+(-1+2\text{i})(-1+\text{i}) & (1-3\text{i})(3+\text{i})+(-1+2\text{i})(1-\text{i}) \\ (2+2\text{i})(3-\text{i})+(1-\text{i})(-1+\text{i}) & (2+2\text{i})(3+\text{i})+(1-\text{i})(1-\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-10\text{i}+(-1-3\text{i}) & (6-8\text{i})+(1+3\text{i}) \\ (8+4\text{i})+2\text{i} & (4+8\text{i})+(-2\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1-13\text{i} & 7-5\text{i} \\ 8+6\text{i} & 4+6\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
Multiplying the matrices using the usual method, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}1-3\text{i} & -1+2\text{i} \\ 2+2\text{i} & 1-\text{i}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3-\text{i} & 3+\text{i} \\ -1+\text{i} & 1-\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(1-3\text{i})(3-\text{i})+(-1+2\text{i})(-1+\text{i}) & (1-3\text{i})(3+\text{i})+(-1+2\text{i})(1-\text{i}) \\ (2+2\text{i})(3-\text{i})+(1-\text{i})(-1+\text{i}) & (2+2\text{i})(3+\text{i})+(1-\text{i})(1-\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-10\text{i}+(-1-3\text{i}) & (6-8\text{i})+(1+3\text{i}) \\ (8+4\text{i})+2\text{i} & (4+8\text{i})+(-2\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1-13\text{i} & 7-5\text{i} \\ 8+6\text{i} & 4+6\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

If A=[−1−i−i3−2+i] and B=[1+i−3i−4−i6], then AB=

a
[−1+2i−3−3i12+i−12−3i]
b
[12+i−3−3i−1+2i−12−3i]
c
[−3−12i−3−3i12+i2−i]
d
[−1+2i−12−3i12+i−3−3i]
e
[−1+2i12+i−3−3i−12−3i]
Submit

decision.explanation: Row-by-column multiplication gives: (−1−i)(1+i)+(−i)(−4−i)=−1+2i; (−1−i)(−3i)+(−i)6=−3−3i; 3(1+i)+(−2+i)(−4−i)=12+i; and 3(−3i)+6(−2+i)=−12−3i. Thus option a matches AB.

after.name: Question 12
after.problem: If $\,A=[\begin{aligned}-1-\text{i} & -\text{i} \\ 3 & -2+\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,B=[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & -3\text{i} \\ -4-\text{i} & 6\end{aligned}]\,$, then $AB=$
after.worked_solution:
Multiplying the matrices using the usual method, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}-1-\text{i} & -\text{i} \\ 3 & -2+\text{i}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & -3\text{i} \\ -4-\text{i} & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(-1-\text{i})(1+\text{i})+(-\text{i})(-4-\text{i}) & (-1-\text{i})(-3\text{i})+(-\text{i})\cdot 6 \\ 3\cdot (1+\text{i})+(-2+\text{i})(-4-\text{i}) & 3\cdot (-3\text{i})+(-2+\text{i})\cdot 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2\text{i}+(4\text{i}-1) & (3\text{i}-3)+(-6\text{i}) \\ (3+3\text{i})+(9-2\text{i}) & (-9\text{i})+(-12+6\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1+2\text{i} & -3-3\text{i} \\ 12+\text{i} & -12-3\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:

$$

$$

decision.explanation: The first entry is (1−i)(5−2i)+(2−2i)(2+i)=(3−7i)+(6−2i)=9−9i. The second is (3−6i)(5−2i)+(3−3i)(2+i)=(3−36i)+(9−3i)=12−39i. This matches option b.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem: If $\,A=[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & 2-2\text{i} \\ 3-6\text{i} & 3-3\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,x=[\begin{aligned}5-2\text{i} \\ 2+\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$, then $\,Ax=$
after.worked_solution:
Multiplying the matrix by the vector using the usual method, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & 2-2\text{i} \\ 3-6\text{i} & 3-3\text{i}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}5-2\text{i} \\ 2+\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(1-\text{i})(5-2\text{i})+(2-2\text{i})(2+\text{i}) \\ (3-6\text{i})(5-2\text{i})+(3-3\text{i})(2+\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(3-7\text{i})+(6-2\text{i}) \\ (3-36\text{i})+(9-3\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9-9\text{i} \\ 12-39\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
Multiplying the matrix by the vector using the usual method, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & 2-2\text{i} \\ 3-6\text{i} & 3-3\text{i}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}5-2\text{i} \\ 2+\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(1-\text{i})(5-2\text{i})+(2-2\text{i})(2+\text{i}) \\ (3-6\text{i})(5-2\text{i})+(3-3\text{i})(2+\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(3-7\text{i})+(6-2\text{i}) \\ (3-36\text{i})+(9-3\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9-9\text{i} \\ 12-39\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Multiplying the matrices using the usual method, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}2+3\text{i} & 1+2\text{i} \\ 2+\text{i} & 4+4\text{i}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3+2\text{i} & 2+\text{i} \\ 1+2\text{i} & 2+2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(2+3\text{i})(3+2\text{i})+(1+2\text{i})(1+2\text{i}) & (2+3\text{i})(2+\text{i})+(1+2\text{i})(2+2\text{i}) \\ (2+\text{i})(3+2\text{i})+(4+4\text{i})(1+2\text{i}) & (2+\text{i})(2+\text{i})+(4+4\text{i})(2+2\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}13\text{i}+(-3+4\text{i}) & (1+8\text{i})+(-2+6\text{i}) \\ (4+7\text{i})+(-4+12\text{i}) & (3+4\text{i})+16\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3+17\text{i} & -1+14\text{i} \\ 19\text{i} & 3+20\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
Multiplying the matrices using the usual method, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}2+3\text{i} & 1+2\text{i} \\ 2+\text{i} & 4+4\text{i}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3+2\text{i} & 2+\text{i} \\ 1+2\text{i} & 2+2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(2+3\text{i})(3+2\text{i})+(1+2\text{i})(1+2\text{i}) & (2+3\text{i})(2+\text{i})+(1+2\text{i})(2+2\text{i}) \\ (2+\text{i})(3+2\text{i})+(4+4\text{i})(1+2\text{i}) & (2+\text{i})(2+\text{i})+(4+4\text{i})(2+2\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}13\text{i}+(-3+4\text{i}) & (1+8\text{i})+(-2+6\text{i}) \\ (4+7\text{i})+(-4+12\text{i}) & (3+4\text{i})+16\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3+17\text{i} & -1+14\text{i} \\ 19\text{i} & 3+20\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The first entry is (1−i)i+(2−i)(−i)+(3−i)(1+i)=(1+i)+(−1−2i)+(4+2i)=4+i. The second is (1+i)i+(1+2i)(−i)+(1+3i)(1+i)=(−1+i)+(2−i)+(−2+4i)=−1+4i. Thus option a is correct.

after.name: Question 15
after.problem: If $\,A=[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & 2-\text{i} & 3-\text{i} \\ 1+\text{i} & 1+2\text{i} & 1+3\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,x=[\begin{aligned}\text{i} \\ -\text{i} \\ 1+\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$, then $\,Ax=$
after.worked_solution:
Multiplying the matrix by the vector using the usual method, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & 2-\text{i} & 3-\text{i} \\ 1+\text{i} & 1+2\text{i} & 1+3\text{i}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\text{i} \\ -\text{i} \\ 1+\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(1-\text{i})(\text{i})+(2-\text{i})(-\text{i})+(3-\text{i})(1+\text{i}) \\ (1+\text{i})(\text{i})+(1+2\text{i})(-\text{i})+(1+3\text{i})(1+\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(1+\text{i})+(-1-2\text{i})+(4+2\text{i}) \\ (-1+\text{i})+(2-\text{i})+(-2+4\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4+\text{i} \\ -1+4\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
Multiplying the matrix by the vector using the usual method, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & 2-\text{i} & 3-\text{i} \\ 1+\text{i} & 1+2\text{i} & 1+3\text{i}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\text{i} \\ -\text{i} \\ 1+\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(1-\text{i})(\text{i})+(2-\text{i})(-\text{i})+(3-\text{i})(1+\text{i}) \\ (1+\text{i})(\text{i})+(1+2\text{i})(-\text{i})+(1+3\text{i})(1+\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(1+\text{i})+(-1-2\text{i})+(4+2\text{i}) \\ (-1+\text{i})+(2-\text{i})+(-2+4\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4+\text{i} \\ -1+4\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 16
after.problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 0 \\ -3 & \text{i}\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following elementary row operations: 

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{3}{1+\text{i}}{R}_{1}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 0 \\ -3 & \text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{3}{1+\text{i}}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 0 \\ -3+\frac{3}{1+\text{i}}\cdot (1+\text{i}) & \text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 0 \\ 0 & \text{i}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result  is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 0 \\ 0 & \text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations to a Complex Matrix
content.problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 0 \\ -3 & \text{i}\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following elementary row operations: 

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{3}{1+\text{i}}{R}_{1}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 0 \\ -3 & \text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{3}{1+\text{i}}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 0 \\ -3+\frac{3}{1+\text{i}}\cdot (1+\text{i}) & \text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 0 \\ 0 & \text{i}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result  is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 0 \\ 0 & \text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 17
after.problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2\text{i}-1 & 0 \\ 2\text{i} & 1\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following  elementary row operations:

$$
{R}_{1}=\frac{1}{2\text{i}-1}{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}={R}_{2}-2\text{i}{R}_{1}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2\text{i}-1 & 0 \\ 2\text{i} & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2\text{i}-1}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2\text{i} & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2\text{i}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result is

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations to a Complex Matrix
content.problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2\text{i}-1 & 0 \\ 2\text{i} & 1\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following  elementary row operations:

$$
{R}_{1}=\frac{1}{2\text{i}-1}{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}={R}_{2}-2\text{i}{R}_{1}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2\text{i}-1 & 0 \\ 2\text{i} & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2\text{i}-1}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2\text{i} & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2\text{i}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result is

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 18
?

Given the matrix A=[1+i1−i−2ii], find the result of applying to A the following elementary row operation: R2:=R2+2i1+iR1

a
[1+i1−i0i]
b
[0i+2−2ii]
c
[1+i1−i−4ii−2]
d
[1+i1−i4ii+2]
e
[1+i1−i0i+2]
Submit

decision.explanation: Since 2i/(1+i)=1+i, the added row is [(1+i)²,(1+i)(1−i)]=[2i,2]. Thus R₂ becomes [0,i+2], while R₁ remains unchanged. This matches option e.

after.name: Question 18
after.problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ -2\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following elementary row operation:

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{2\text{i}}{1+\text{i}}{R}_{1}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ -2\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{2\text{i}}{1+\text{i}}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ -2\text{i}+\frac{2\text{i}(1+\text{i})}{1+\text{i}} & \text{i}+\frac{2\text{i}(1-\text{i})}{1+\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ -2\text{i}+2\text{i} & \text{i}+\frac{2(\text{i}+1)}{1+\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ 0 & \text{i}+2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result  is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ 0 & \text{i}+2\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 18
?

Given the matrix A=[1+i1−i−2ii], find the result of applying to A the following elementary row operation: R2:=R2+2i1+iR1

a
[1+i1−i0i]
b
[0i+2−2ii]
c
[1+i1−i−4ii−2]
d
[1+i1−i4ii+2]
e
[1+i1−i0i+2]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's apply the row operations to A:

A=[1+i1−i−2ii]R2:=R2+2i1+iR1∼[1+i1−i−2i+2i(1+i)1+ii+2i(1−i)1+i]=[1+i1−i−2i+2ii+2(i+1)1+i]=[1+i1−i0i+2].

Therefore, the result is [1+i1−i0i+2].

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations to a Complex Matrix
content.problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ -2\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following elementary row operation:

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{2\text{i}}{1+\text{i}}{R}_{1}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ -2\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{2\text{i}}{1+\text{i}}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ -2\text{i}+\frac{2\text{i}(1+\text{i})}{1+\text{i}} & \text{i}+\frac{2\text{i}(1-\text{i})}{1+\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ -2\text{i}+2\text{i} & \text{i}+\frac{2(\text{i}+1)}{1+\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ 0 & \text{i}+2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result  is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ 0 & \text{i}+2\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 19

Given the matrix A=[−ii73−2i], find the result of applying to A the following elementary row operations: R2:=R2+7iR1

a
[−ii010−2i]
b
[ii18i]
c
[−1108]
d
[−ii110−2i]
e
[−ii08i]
Submit

decision.explanation: Multiplying R₁ by 7/i gives [−7,7]. Adding this to R₂ gives [7−7,3−2i+7]=[0,10−2i], while R₁ remains unchanged. This matches option a.

after.name: Question 19
after.problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 7 & 3-2\text{i}\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following elementary row operations: 

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{7}{\text{i}}{R}_{1}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 7 & 3-2\text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{7}{\text{i}}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 7+(-\text{i})\cdot \frac{7}{\text{i}} & \text{(}3-2\text{i})+i\cdot \frac{7}{\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 0 & 10-2\text{i}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result  is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 0 & 10-2\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

EXPLANATION

Let's apply the row operations to A:

A=[−ii73−2i]R2:=R2+7iR1∼[−ii7+(−i)⋅7i(3−2i)+i⋅7i]∼[−ii010−2i]

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations to a Complex Matrix
content.problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 7 & 3-2\text{i}\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following elementary row operations: 

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{7}{\text{i}}{R}_{1}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 7 & 3-2\text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{7}{\text{i}}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 7+(-\text{i})\cdot \frac{7}{\text{i}} & \text{(}3-2\text{i})+i\cdot \frac{7}{\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 0 & 10-2\text{i}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result  is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 0 & 10-2\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

Given the matrix A=[1+2i1+i−2+ii], find the result of applying to A the following elementary row operation: R2:=R2+2−i1+2iR1

a
[1+2i1+i11]
b
[1+2i1+i01]
c

d
[1+2i1+iii]
e
[1+2i1+i0i]
Submit

decision.explanation: Since (2−i)/(1+2i)=−i, the added row is [2−i,1−i]. Adding it to [−2+i,i] gives [0,1]. The first row stays unchanged, matching option b.

after.name: Question 20
after.problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 1+\text{i} \\ -2+\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following elementary row operation:

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{2-\text{i}}{1+2\text{i}}{R}_{1}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 1+\text{i} \\ -2+\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{2-\text{i}}{1+2\text{i}}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 1+\text{i} \\ -2+\text{i}+\frac{(2-\text{i})(1+2\text{i})}{1+2\text{i}} & \text{i}+\frac{(2-\text{i})(1+\text{i})}{1+2\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 1+\text{i} \\ 0 & \frac{(\text{i}-2)+(3+\text{i})}{1+2\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 1+\text{i} \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result  is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 1+\text{i} \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

a
[1+2i1+i11]
b
[1+2i1+i01]
c
[1−2i1+ii1]
d
[1+2i1+iii]
e
[1+2i1+i0i]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's apply the row operations to A:

A=[1+2i1+i−2+ii]R2:=R2+2−i1+2iR1∼[1+2i1+i−2+i+(2−i)(1+2i)1+2ii+(2−i)(1+i)1+2i]=[1+2i1+i0(i−2)+(3+i)1+2i]=[1+2i1+i01].

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations to a Complex Matrix
content.problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 1+\text{i} \\ -2+\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following elementary row operation:

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{2-\text{i}}{1+2\text{i}}{R}_{1}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 1+\text{i} \\ -2+\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{2-\text{i}}{1+2\text{i}}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 1+\text{i} \\ -2+\text{i}+\frac{(2-\text{i})(1+2\text{i})}{1+2\text{i}} & \text{i}+\frac{(2-\text{i})(1+\text{i})}{1+2\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 1+\text{i} \\ 0 & \frac{(\text{i}-2)+(3+\text{i})}{1+2\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 1+\text{i} \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result  is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 1+\text{i} \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
